title: Coral: a team of agents, one board, your phone
thesis: Agents from different vendors work as one team on one board, and you steer it from any browser, your phone included.
audience: Developers already running Claude Code, Codex or similar CLIs; watching muted in the README or a feed.
sound: silent; captions only; cuts on the board post and the approve tap
note: STAGED, and said so: a throwaway Coral on an isolated data folder with sample data and scripted mock agents (named by role: Orchestrator, Developer, Reviewer). Board posts are sent by a script in real time and the diff is a real git commit in a throwaway repo; vendor names are not shown on the rows because the mocks are not real Codex or Gemini. Time is compressed where a cut is visible. Nothing is shown that Coral cannot do. The palette is a placeholder until stills of the real dashboard exist.

openQuestions.note: Mocks are repeatable and spend no tokens, but are not the vendors' real CLIs, so the film cannot show vendor names or logos honestly.
openQuestions.pick: Mocks, labelled by role; one real-run clip can follow.
